newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- cash flat, futures higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- cash flat, futures higher.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond secondary market prices were flat to slightly firmer at midday, while the futures markets showed strong gains.
Traders said the cash market is mostly quiet, waiting for a 1415 EST announcement from the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

The Fed is widely expected to announce a 25-basis point increase in short-term rates, although a handful of economists said they expect no change in interest rates since economic indicators continue to show no sign of inflation.

Ahead of the announcement, the government long bond was up 9/32 at 96-17/32 to yield 6.90 percent, with traders attributing the rise to rumors that the Fed would hold steady despite economists' predictions for a tightening.

In new issue action Tuesday, Smith Barney Inc. repriced Delaware State Housing Authority's $43 million bond deal, lowering yields five basis points in some maturities. To see the repricing scale, double click on nN25264635.
On the competitive side, Prudential Securities Inc. won $39 million Connecticut Health and Educational Facilities Authority bonds, reoffering the 2017 maturity at a 5.642 percent yield.

In the futures markets, the June municipal bond futures contract rose 14/32 to 113-24/32, while the June Treasury bond contract jumped 15/32 to 109-14/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 138 ticks from 139 at the close on Monday.
In secondary market activity, Dade County, Fla., water and sewer system revenue bonds of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.78 percent, down one basis point from Monday.
Jefferson County, Ala., sewer revenue bonds of February 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.82 percent, down two basis points.
